title: KV synthetic compaction guided by access signatures
creator: Lina Chen
description: Problem statement: GPU-resident KV cache fragmentation is increasing effective memory pressure for large chat workloads. Continuous batching amplifies fragmentation because variable sequence lengths and interleaved access patterns leave partially-filled KV slots, reducing achievable batch sizes and increasing tail latency. This ticket scopes a pragmatic allocation + soft-compaction strategy driven by lightweight 'access signatures' (a short fingerprint of request access patterns) to reorganize KV resident regions with minimal jitter to latency SLOs. Goals: 1) reduce fragmentation measured as fraction of unusable KV bytes by >=40% on long-running hosts; 2) keep p50/p95 token generation latency regression <=3% and p99 <=5%; 3) avoid pauses >10ms on request hot path by pushing heavy work to background microcompaction and opportunistic slices.
decisions: Use a two-tier approach: fast inline allocation that records per-allocation 'access signature' and a background synthetic compactor that prefers co-locating allocations with similar signatures.
Encode access signature as 64-bit hash of (sequence_length_bucket, model_variant_id, prefix_token_hash mod 1024) with aging applied every 30s.
Avoid global stop-the-world compaction; instead perform micro-relocation at compaction-safe safepoints tied to GPU kernel boundaries and batch completion events.
Prioritize eviction of low-reuse signatures for immediate reclamation under memory pressure; schedule relocation for mid-reuse signatures during idle GPU cycles.
Expose a runtime knob 'kv.compaction_throttle' to control background relocation bandwidth and a 'kv.signature_granularity' to tune sensitivity.
First rollout will be behind runtime feature-flag 'kv.synthetic_compaction_v1' for A/B testing on Dedicated nodes.
tradeoffs: Synthetic compaction improves long-term memory utilization but can add background GPU cycles and extra memcpy traffic; we accept a small throughput overhead during low-utilization windows to gain headroom for larger batches.
Co-locating by signature can increase misplacement for rare long-tail patterns; we mitigate with fallback heuristics that pin very-hot allocations to exempted hot pools.
Finer-grained signatures reduce fragmentation but increase metadata overhead; the chosen 64-bit compact signature balances accuracy vs. metadata footprint.
Implementing relocation on-device avoids PCIe transfer overhead but adds kernel complexity; initial implementation will use device-to-device memcpy primitives available in our CUDA runtime.
Delaying compaction until safe points reduces user-visible jitter but defers reclamation; we accept slightly higher short-term memory pressure for smoother latencies.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): add signature generation to allocation hot path, collect telemetry counters and histogram of signature reuse and fragmentation metric per-GPU.

Phase 2 (prototype, 2 weeks): implement background micro-relocator that picks candidate slots and uses device memcpy to consolidate same-signature allocations into contiguous regions; include compaction_throttle and safepoint hooks.
Phase 3 (integration, 1 week): wire prototype into Continuous Batcher so relocations are scheduled after batch completions and during kBatchIdle windows; add feature-flag and rollout gating.
Phase 4 (validation, 1 week): run large-scale replay tests on staging with mixed seq-length workloads, tune thresholds and signature buckets, capture latency and memory metrics.
Phase 5 (rollout): enable for 10% of Dedicated nodes, monitor telemetry for regressions, gradually increase to 100% after validation.
testing_plan: Unit tests for signature computation determinism and bucket stability.
Integration test that simulates interleaved chat sessions with controlled sequence length distribution to measure fragmentation before/after compaction.
Load replay on staging (3-day run) using production traces to ensure p99 latency meets SLOs under feature-flag on/off comparisons.
Chaos test: induce sudden memory pressure and verify relocation prioritization and grace under eviction without crashes.
GPU profiler run to ensure background memcpy kernels don't block inference kernels and remain within throttle budget.
rollout_plan: Enable 'kv.synthetic_compaction_v1' on Canary pool (5 nodes) for 48h, gather telemetry and logs.
If metrics show expected fragmentation drop and <5% p99 regression, expand to 10% pool for 7 days.
Automated rollback if p99 increases >10% or OOM events occur.
Post-rollout: create runbook summarizing observed compaction bandwidth and recommended defaults for kv.compaction_throttle per hardware class.
telemetry: New gauge: kv.fragmentation_ratio (per-GPU): fraction of KV bytes currently unusable due to fragmentation.
Histogram: kv.signature_reuse_count (per-signature) to identify hot signatures.
Latency buckets tied to 'kv.compaction_active' label to correlate relocations with user-visible tail latency.
Dashboards: compaction dashboard in Console under runtime-kv-ops with alert if fragmentation_ratio > 0.35 for >10m.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Lina Chen: Spike results show initial signature reuse is highly clustered; top 10 signatures account for ~60% of live allocations on chat-xxlarge models.
2026-03-04 - Marco Rivera: Prototype relocation uses cudaMemcpyAsync with stream prioritization; observed 8-12% extra device bandwidth during idle windows on A100 which seems acceptable.
2026-03-06 - Juliet Park (PM): Please ensure a clear toggle for Dedicated customers and add a migration warning for nodes with custom allocator tweaks.
2026-03-09 - Security review: Reviewed and no PCIe host memory copies introduced; background ops run on-device. No further action required. (Security team)
2026-03-11 - QA: Running replay for 48h on staging; initial numbers: fragmentation_ratio dropped from 0.47 -> 0.26, p99 latency steady at +2.8%. Continuing extended run.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation ratio reduction >= 40% on representative staging traces compared to baseline.
No more than 5% regression in p99 inference latency under mixed workloads during the 48h staging run.
No increase in GPU out-of-memory events attributable to compaction logic during rollout.
Monitoring and alerts in Console are populated and validated; runbook updated.
